query: The Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy previously showed limited amorphous retention and a complicated thermal response. Earlier thermal studies of Ni–P and Pd–Ni–P alloys found that rapid quenching could produce amorphous material, but that its stability was limited during subsequent heating. The design challenge is therefore to obtain robust glass formation across relevant cooling conditions without sacrificing stability during reheating. What single intervention could improve amorphous retention and thermal stability during solidification and thermal analysis? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted outcome relative to the reported behavior of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20, the cooling-rate and reheating conditions under which it should or should not succeed, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing 2 at.% of Mn with B to form the alloy Cr16Mn14Fe16Co16Ni16P20B2 will increase melt viscosity and suppress atomic diffusion, so that (a) the critical cooling-rate for glass formation drops by roughly one order of magnitude and (b) the first crystallisation event during reheating is shifted ≈50 K higher than in the parent Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic high-entropy base Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16 with 20 at.% P; fabricated by induction melting to a homogeneous liquid at 1470 °C.
generation.intervention: Introduce 2 at.% B at the expense of Mn (Cr16Mn14Fe16Co16Ni16P20B2). No other processing changes.
generation.conditions: Rapid solidification by melt–spinning in 0.04 MPa Ar; wheel speeds adjusted to give surface-contact cooling rates between 10³ and 10⁵ K s⁻¹. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) on 5 mg ribbons at 20 K min⁻¹ up to 800 °C in flowing Ar.
generation.structural_mediator: Short-range B–P and B–transition-metal covalent/metallic clusters that increase packing efficiency and frustrate crystal nucleation.
generation.mechanism: Boron introduces (1) strong directional B–P and B–M bonds that raise melt viscosity, (2) negative heats of mixing and atomic-size mismatch that deepen the eutectic, and (3) additional topological frustration. Combined, these lower the nucleation frequency during quenching and slow atomic rearrangements on heating, expanding the super-cooled liquid region.
generation.predicted_outcome: 1. Fully amorphous ribbons will be obtained at ~10⁴ K s⁻¹ instead of >10⁵ K s⁻¹. 2. DSC will show the onset of primary crystallisation (T_x1) near 500 ± 10 °C, ~50 K above the ~450 °C reported for Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20. 3. At very slow cooling (≤10³ K s⁻¹) the alloy will still crystallise, and B contents ≥5 at.% will re-induce brittleness and early boride precipitation, so benefits will vanish outside 1–3 at.% B.
generation.baseline: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 requires ≳10⁵ K s⁻¹ to retain >80 % amorphous fraction and crystallises during DSC at ~450 °C with a narrow super-cooled liquid region (<25 K).
generation.boundary: The effect is expected only for 1–3 at.% B and cooling rates between 10³ and 10⁵ K s⁻¹; outside this window (very slow cooling or high B) crystalline or brittle phases dominate.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate—no published data exist yet for B additions to this specific 6-element HEA-glass; quantitative shifts (one order of magnitude in R_c, 50 K in T_x) are estimates extrapolated from Ni–P–B and Fe–Cr–P–B glass formers.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of melt-spun ribbons: (i) baseline Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 and (ii) Cr16Mn14Fe16Co16Ni16P20B2. Produce ribbons at wheel speeds giving ~10⁴ K s⁻¹ cooling. Characterise phase state and thermal stability.
measurements: X-ray diffraction for amorphous halo vs crystalline peaks
Differential scanning calorimetry (20 K min⁻¹) to measure glass-transition (T_g) and crystallisation onset (T_x1)
Transmission electron microscopy to confirm amorphous structure
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if (a) the B-containing ribbons show ≤80 % amorphous fraction by XRD/TEM at 10⁴ K s⁻¹ or (b) the first DSC crystallisation onset is not at least 30 K higher than that of the baseline alloy.
